title.zh: 卷三百九十二 列傳第一百五十一 趙汝愚子:崇憲
title.en: Volume 392 Biographies 151: Zhao Ruyu and Son: Chongxian
title.raw: 卷三百九十二 列傳第一百五十一 趙汝愚子:崇憲 Volume 392 Biographies 151: Zhao Ruyu and Son: Chongxian

sentences.zh: 趙汝愚

translations.literal: Zhao Ruyu
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ruyu

sentences.zh: 趙汝愚，字子直，漢恭憲王元佐七世孫，居饒之餘干縣。

translations.literal: Zhao Ruyu, courtesy name Zizhi, was a seventh-generation descendant of Prince Gongxian of Han, Yuanzuo, and dwelt in Yugan County in Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ruyu, styled Zizhi, was seven generations removed from Prince Gongxian of Han, Yuanzuo, and made his home in Yugan County, Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 父善應，字彥遠，官終修武郎、江西兵馬都監。

translations.literal: His father Shanying, courtesy name Yanyuan, ended his career as Gentleman for Cultivating Martial Virtue and Commander of Military and Horse Affairs of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shanying, styled Yanyuan, rose no higher than Gentleman for Cultivating Martial Virtue and Jiangxi Commander of Military and Horse Affairs.

sentences.zh: 性純孝，親病，嘗刺血和藥以進。

translations.literal: By nature he was thoroughly filial; when his parents fell ill, he once drew his own blood to mix into medicine and presented it to them.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply filial by nature. When his parents were ill, he once pricked his finger and mixed the blood into their medicine before serving it.

sentences.zh: 母畏雷，每聞雷則披衣走其所。

translations.literal: His mother feared thunder; whenever thunder sounded he would throw on his clothes and run to where she was.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was afraid of thunder, and at every peal he would throw on his clothes and hurry to her side.

sentences.zh: 嘗寒夜遠歸，從者將扣門，遽止之曰：「無恐吾母。」

translations.literal: Once on a cold night he returned from afar; when his attendants were about to knock at the gate, he suddenly stopped them, saying, "Do not frighten my mother."
translations.idiomatic: Once he came home late on a bitter night. As his attendants were about to knock at the door, he stopped them at once: "Don't startle my mother."

sentences.zh: 露坐達明，門啟而後入。

translations.literal: He sat in the open until dawn and only entered after the gate was opened.
translations.idiomatic: He sat in the open air until daybreak and went in only after the gate was opened.

sentences.zh: 家貧，諸弟未制衣不敢制，已制未服不敢服，一瓜果之微必相待共嘗之。

translations.literal: The family was poor; if his younger brothers had not yet had clothes made, he dared not have any made; if clothes were made but not yet worn, he dared not wear them; even the smallest fruit or melon had to be waited for so they could taste it together.
translations.idiomatic: The household was poor. He would not have clothes made until his younger brothers had theirs, nor wear new garments until they did, and even the humblest melon or fruit had to be shared before anyone tasted it.

sentences.zh: 母喪，哭泣嘔血，毀瘠骨立，終日俯首柩傍，聞雷猶起，側立垂涕。

translations.literal: At his mother's death he wept until he vomited blood, wasted away until only skin and bone remained, bowed his head beside the bier all day long, and still rose at thunder, standing to one side with tears falling.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he wept until he brought up blood, wasted to skin and bone, and spent the whole day bowed beside her coffin. He still rose at thunder, standing aside with tears streaming down.

sentences.zh: 既終喪，言及其親，未嘗不揮涕，生朝必哭於廟。

translations.literal: After the mourning period ended, whenever he spoke of his parents he never failed to brush away tears; on their birthdays he was sure to weep at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Even after mourning was over, mention of his parents never failed to move him to tears, and on their birthdays he always wept at the family shrine.

sentences.zh: 父終肺疾，每膳不忍以諸肺爲羞。

translations.literal: His father died of lung disease; at every meal he could not bear to serve any lung dish.
translations.idiomatic: His father had died of lung disease, and at every meal he refused to set out dishes made from lung.

sentences.zh: 母生歲值卯，謂卯兔神也，終其身不食兔。

translations.literal: His mother was born in a year of the mao branch; he said mao was the spirit of the rabbit, and for his whole life he did not eat rabbit.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had been born in a mao year, which he held to be the sign of the rabbit spirit, and he never ate rabbit meat as long as he lived.

sentences.zh: 聞四方水旱，輒憂形於色。

translations.literal: Whenever he heard of flood or drought in the four directions, worry showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: News of flood or drought anywhere in the realm always showed plainly on his face.

sentences.zh: 江、淮警報至，爲之流涕，不食累日；

translations.literal: When alarms came from the Jiang and Huai regions, he wept for it and went without food for many days.
translations.idiomatic: When alarms arrived from the Jiang and Huai frontiers, he wept and went without food for days on end.

sentences.zh: 同僚會宴，善應悵然曰：「此寧諸君樂飲時耶！」

translations.literal: At a gathering banquet with colleagues, Shanying said sadly, "Is this really the time for you gentlemen to drink in pleasure?"
translations.idiomatic: At a colleagues' banquet he said bleakly, "Is this really a time for you to be drinking and making merry?"

sentences.zh: 衆爲失色而罷。

translations.literal: The company turned pale and broke up.
translations.idiomatic: The others turned pale and the feast broke up.

sentences.zh: 故人之孤女，貧無所歸，善應聘以爲己子婦。

translations.literal: An old friend's orphaned daughter, poor with nowhere to go, Shanying took in marriage for his own son.
translations.idiomatic: A friend's orphaned daughter, left destitute with nowhere to turn, he took as his own son's wife.

sentences.zh: 有嘗同僚者死不克葬，子傭食他所，善應馳往哭之，歸其子而予之貲，使葬焉。

translations.literal: A former colleague died and could not be buried; his son hired himself out for food elsewhere. Shanying hurried to weep over the corpse, brought the son back, gave him funds, and had the burial carried out.
translations.idiomatic: A former colleague died too poor for burial while his son worked as a hired hand far away. Shanying rushed to mourn the body, brought the son home, gave him money, and saw the funeral done.

sentences.zh: 道見病者必收恤之，躬爲煮藥。

translations.literal: On the road, whenever he saw the sick he would take them in and care for them, personally boiling medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he met the sick on the road he took them in and tended them himself, even boiling their medicine.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，旦夕率其家人輟食之半，以飼饑者。

translations.literal: In years of famine, morning and evening he led his household to give up half their food to feed the hungry.
translations.idiomatic: In famine years he had his family give up half their meals morning and evening to feed the starving.

sentences.zh: 夏不去草，冬不破壤，懼百蟲之遊且蟄者失其所也。

translations.literal: In summer he did not pull up grass; in winter he did not break the soil, fearing that the hundred insects roaming or hibernating would lose their places.
translations.idiomatic: In summer he would not weed, in winter he would not break ground, lest he disturb insects abroad or in their winter burrows.

sentences.zh: 晉陵尤袤稱之曰：「古君子也。」

translations.literal: You Mao of Jinling praised him, saying, "A gentleman of antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: You Mao of Jinling called him "a gentleman of the old school."

sentences.zh: 既卒，丞相陳俊卿題其墓碣曰：「宋篤行趙公彥遠之墓」。

translations.literal: After his death, Chief Councillor Chen Junqing inscribed his tomb tablet: "Tomb of Zhao Gong Yanyuan of the Song, of devoted conduct."
translations.idiomatic: After he died, Chief Councillor Chen Junqing inscribed his tombstone: "Tomb of Zhao Gong Yanyuan of the Song, a man of steadfast virtue."

sentences.zh: 汝愚早有大志，每曰：「丈夫得汗青一幅紙，始不負此生。」

translations.literal: Ruyu early had great ambition and often said, "A man who wins one sheet on the green silk of history has not lived this life in vain."
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu had lofty ambitions from youth and often said, "A man has not wasted his life until he earns a line on history's green silk."

sentences.zh: 擢進士第一，簽書寧國軍節度判官，召試館職，除祕書省正字。

translations.literal: He was placed first among jinshi graduates, signed as military administration secretary of Ningguo Army, was summoned to the examination for institute posts, and was appointed rectifier in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He took first place in the jinshi examination, served as signing secretary on the Ningguo military commission, passed the institute examination, and was made rectifier in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 孝宗方銳意恢復，始見，即陳自治之策，孝宗稱善，遷校書郎。

translations.literal: Xiaozong was then keen on recovery; at their first meeting Ruyu at once set forth a policy of self-strengthening. Xiaozong praised it and promoted him to collator.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong was then bent on reconquest. At their first audience Ruyu laid out a program of internal reform, which the emperor praised, and he was made collator.

sentences.zh: 知閤門張說擢簽書樞密院事，汝愚不往見，率同列請祠，未報。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Gate Zhang Yue was promoted to signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Ruyu did not go to call on him, led his colleagues in requesting temple posts, and received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yue, director of the palace gate, was promoted to sign the Bureau of Military Affairs, Ruyu refused to pay his respects and led his colleagues in asking for temple appointments. No answer came.

sentences.zh: 會祖母訃至，即日歸，因自劾，上不加罪。

translations.literal: When word came of his grandmother's death, he returned home that same day and submitted a self-impeachment; the emperor did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: News of his grandmother's death arrived and he went home the same day, impeaching himself in the process. The emperor did not penalize him.

sentences.zh: 遷著作郎、知信州，易台州，除江西轉運判官，入爲吏部郎兼太子侍講。

translations.literal: He was moved to compiler, made prefect of Xinzhou, transferred to Taizhou, appointed transport commissioner of Jiangxi, and entered the capital as a director in the Ministry of Personnel and concurrent lecturer to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to compiler, governed Xinzhou, was transferred to Taizhou, then made Jiangxi transport commissioner before entering the capital as director in the Ministry of Personnel and lecturer to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 遷祕書少監兼權給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice-director of the Secretariat and acting supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice-director of the Secretariat with acting rank as supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 內侍陳源有寵于德壽宮，添差浙西副總管。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Chen Yuan had favor at the Deposed Sovereign's Palace and was given an additional appointment as deputy overall commander of western Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Chen Yuan, a favorite at Gaozong's retired palace, was given an extra post as deputy overall commander in western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 汝愚言：「祖宗以童貫典兵，卒開邊釁，源不宜使居總戎之任。」

translations.literal: Ruyu said, "Our ancestors, by putting Tong Guan in charge of troops, in the end opened border troubles; Yuan should not be allowed to hold overall military command."
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu argued, "The founders put Tong Guan over the army and in the end provoked war on the frontier. Chen Yuan must not hold supreme military command."

sentences.zh: 孝宗喜，詔自今內侍不得兼兵職。

translations.literal: Xiaozong was pleased and decreed that from then on inner attendants might not concurrently hold military posts.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong was pleased and ordered that eunuchs were henceforth barred from military office.

sentences.zh: 舊制，密院文書皆經門下省，張說在西府，託言邊機不宜泄。

translations.literal: By old regulation, documents of the Bureau of Military Affairs all passed through the Secretariat-Chancellery; Zhang Yue in the western office pleaded that frontier affairs should not be leaked.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, Military Affairs documents all went through the Secretariat. Zhang Yue in the western office claimed frontier business must not be disclosed.

sentences.zh: 汝愚謂：「東西二府朝廷治亂所關，中書庶政無一不由東省，何密院不然？」

translations.literal: Ruyu said, "The eastern and western offices bear on whether the court is well or ill governed; in the Secretariat no ordinary affair fails to pass through the eastern office—why should the Bureau of Military Affairs be different?"
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu replied, "The two offices govern the fate of the dynasty. Every routine matter in the Secretariat passes through the eastern office—why should Military Affairs be exempt?"

sentences.zh: 孝宗命如舊制。

translations.literal: Xiaozong ordered a return to the old regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong restored the old practice.

sentences.zh: 權吏部侍郎兼太子右庶子，論知閤王抃招權預政，出抃外祠。

translations.literal: As acting vice-minister of Personnel and concurrent right tutor to the heir apparent, he impeached Director of the Palace Gate Wang Bian for grasping power and interfering in government, and Bian was sent to an outer temple post.
translations.idiomatic: As acting vice-minister of Personnel and right tutor to the heir apparent, he charged Palace Gate director Wang Bian with seizing power in government, and Wang was sent to a temple post outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 以集英殿修撰帥福建，陛辭，言國事之大者四，其一謂：「吳氏四世專蜀兵，非國家之利，請及今以漸抑之。」

translations.literal: As compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence he commanded Fujian; at his farewell audience he spoke of four great matters of state, the first saying, "The Wu family for four generations has monopolized Shu troops—this is not to the state's advantage; I ask that they be gradually restrained while there is still time."
translations.idiomatic: Made compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence and commander in Fujian, he took leave with four major policy points, the first being: "Four generations of the Wu clan have held Sichuan's armies—a danger to the realm. Please begin restraining them now, step by step."

sentences.zh: 進直學士、制置四川兼知成都府。

translations.literal: He was advanced to academician in regular attendance, made commissioner for Sichuan, and concurrently prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to academician in regular attendance, made Sichuan commissioner, and concurrently prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 諸羌蠻相挻爲邊患，汝愚至，悉以計分其勢。

translations.literal: The various Qiang and Man tribes stirred one another into frontier trouble; when Ruyu arrived, he used stratagems in every case to divide their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang and Man tribes were inciting one another along the border. Ruyu arrived and in each case used strategy to split their power.

sentences.zh: 孝宗謂其有文武威風，召還。

translations.literal: Xiaozong said he had the martial and civil authority of a commanding presence and summoned him back.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong judged him to possess both civil and military authority and recalled him to court.

sentences.zh: 光宗受禪，趣召未至，殿中侍御史范處義論其稽命，除知潭州，辭，改太平州。

translations.literal: When Guangzong received the abdication, an urgent summons was sent but Ruyu had not yet arrived; Palace Attendant Fan Chuyi impeached him for delaying his orders; he was appointed prefect of Tanzhou, declined, and was changed to Taipingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong took the throne, an urgent recall was issued before Ruyu arrived. Palace attendant Fan Chuyi charged him with tardiness. He was named prefect of Tanzhou, declined, and was given Taipingzhou instead.

sentences.zh: 進敷文閣學士，知福州。

translations.literal: He was advanced to academician of the Hall for Spreading Culture and made prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made academician of the Hall for Spreading Culture and prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹熙二年，召爲吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxi he was summoned as minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxi year 2 he was recalled as minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 先是，高宗以宮人黃氏侍光宗於東宮，及即位爲貴妃，后李氏意不能平。

translations.literal: Earlier, Gaozong had given the palace woman Lady Huang to attend Guangzong in the Eastern Palace; when he took the throne she became honored consort, and Empress Li could not be at ease in her mind.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Gaozong had placed the palace lady Huang in Guangzong's household as heir. When he became emperor she was made honored consort, and Empress Li was deeply unsettled.

sentences.zh: 是年冬十一月郊，有司已戒而風雨暴至，光宗震懼，及齋宿青城，貴妃暴薨，駕還，聞之恚，是夕疾作。

translations.literal: That winter in the eleventh month at the suburban sacrifice, the offices had already issued warnings when violent wind and rain came; Guangzong was shaken with fear. While he was fasting and lodging at Qingcheng, the honored consort died suddenly. When the imperial carriage returned and he heard of it, he was enraged, and that night his illness began.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, as the suburban rites approached in the eleventh month, a sudden storm struck though the ritual officers had already proclaimed the fast. Guangzong was terrified. While he kept ritual seclusion at Qingcheng, the honored consort died suddenly. On his return he flew into a rage, and that night he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 內侍馳白孝宗，孝宗倉卒至南內，問所以致疾之由，不免有所戒責。

translations.literal: An inner attendant galloped to inform Xiaozong; Xiaozong hurried to the Southern Palace, asked the cause of the illness, and could not avoid some admonition and reproof.
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch raced to tell Xiaozong, who hurried to the Southern Palace, asked what had brought on the illness, and could not refrain from scolding him.

sentences.zh: 及光宗疾稍平，汝愚入對。

translations.literal: When Guangzong's illness had eased somewhat, Ruyu entered for audience.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong's illness eased slightly, Ruyu had an audience.

sentences.zh: 上常以五日一朝孝宗于重華宮，至是往往以傳旨免，至會慶節上壽，駕不出，冬至朝賀又不出，都人以爲憂。

translations.literal: The emperor had customarily on the fifth day paid court to Xiaozong at Chonghua Palace; by this time he often excused himself by transmitted order. At the Festival of Joint Celebration for the birthday felicitation the carriage did not go out; at the winter solstice court congratulations again he did not go out, and the people of the capital were troubled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had customarily visited Xiaozong at Chonghua Palace every five days, but now often excused himself by written order. He stayed away from the birthday felicitation at the Festival of Joint Celebration, and again from the winter solstice audience. The capital was full of anxiety.

sentences.zh: 汝愚往復規諫，上意乃悟。

translations.literal: Ruyu went back and forth with remonstrance and admonition, and the emperor's mind was awakened.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu remonstrated again and again until the emperor came to his senses.

sentences.zh: 汝愚又屬嗣秀王伯圭調護，於是兩宮之情通。

translations.literal: Ruyu also entrusted the heir apparent's younger brother, Prince of Xiuxiu Bogui, to mediate and care for them, and thus feeling between the two palaces was opened.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu also asked Prince Xiuxiu Bogui to help reconcile them, and feeling between the two courts was restored.

sentences.zh: 光宗及后俱詣北內，從容竟日。

translations.literal: Guangzong and the empress both went to the Northern Palace and passed the day at ease together.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzong and the empress both visited the Northern Palace and spent a leisurely day there.

sentences.zh: 四年，汝愚知貢舉，與監察御史汪義端有違言。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Ruyu supervised the metropolitan examination and had words of dispute with investigating censor Wang Yiduan.
translations.idiomatic: In year four Ruyu ran the metropolitan examinations and clashed with investigating censor Wang Yiduan.

sentences.zh: 汝愚除同知樞密院事，義端言祖宗之法，宗室不爲執政，詆汝愚植黨沽名，疏上，不納。

translations.literal: Ruyu was appointed associate controller of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Yiduan said that by the law of the ancestors, members of the imperial clan did not serve as chief ministers, slandered Ruyu for forming factions and trading on reputation, submitted a memorial, and it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu was made associate controller of Military Affairs. Yiduan cited ancestral law forbidding imperial clansmen in high office and accused Ruyu of faction-building and self-promotion. His memorial was ignored.

sentences.zh: 又論臺諫、給舍陰附汝愚，一切緘默，不報。

translations.literal: He again argued that censors, remonstrators, and supervising secretaries secretly sided with Ruyu and were altogether silent; no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He charged that censors and supervising secretaries were secretly backing Ruyu and keeping silent. Again no reply.

sentences.zh: 論汝愚發策譏訕祖宗，又不報。

translations.literal: He argued that in the examination questions Ruyu had mocked the ancestors; again no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed Ruyu's examination questions had mocked the founders. Still no reply.

sentences.zh: 汝愚力辭，上爲徙義端軍器監。

translations.literal: Ruyu strongly declined the post; the emperor moved Yiduan to the Directorate of Armaments for him.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu firmly declined the appointment, and the emperor transferred Yiduan to the Directorate of Armaments.

sentences.zh: 給事中黃裳言：「汝愚事親孝，事君忠，居官廉，憂國愛民，出於天性。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Huang Shang said, "Ruyu is filial to parents, loyal to his ruler, incorrupt in office, and cares for the state and loves the people from his inborn nature.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Huang Shang wrote, "Ruyu is filial to his parents, loyal to his sovereign, incorrupt in office, and cares for the realm and its people by nature.

sentences.zh: 義端實忌賢，不可以不黜。」

translations.literal: Yiduan truly envies the worthy and must be dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: Yiduan is truly jealous of talent and must be removed."

sentences.zh: 上乃黜義端補郡，汝愚不獲已拜命。

translations.literal: The emperor then dismissed Yiduan to a prefectural post, and Ruyu had no choice but to accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed Yiduan to a prefecture, and Ruyu accepted the post with reluctance.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷知樞密院事，辭不拜，有旨趣受告。

translations.literal: Before long he was moved to controller of the Bureau of Military Affairs, declined and did not accept, and an order urged him to take the notice of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to controller of Military Affairs. He declined but an imperial order pressed him to accept.

sentences.zh: 汝愚對曰：「臣非敢久辭。

translations.literal: Ruyu replied, "Your servant does not dare to decline for long.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu answered, "I do not mean to refuse for long.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗論朝廷數事，其言未見用，今陛下過重華，留正復相，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Your servant once discussed several matters of the court whose words were not adopted; now Your Majesty has passed Chonghua, Liu Zheng is again chief minister—the realm is greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: I have urged several policies that went unheeded. Now that Your Majesty has visited Chonghua and Liu Zheng is chief minister again, the realm is greatly blessed.

sentences.zh: 惟武興未除帥，臣心不敢安。」

translations.literal: Only Wuxing has not yet had its commander removed; your servant's heart dares not be at ease."
translations.idiomatic: Only the Wuxing command still lacks a new general, and I cannot rest easy until that is settled."

sentences.zh: 上遂以張詔代領武興軍，汝愚乃受命。

translations.literal: The emperor then had Zhang Zhao take over the Wuxing Army in his place, and Ruyu then accepted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replaced the Wuxing commander with Zhang Zhao, and Ruyu then took office.

sentences.zh: 光宗之疾生於疑畏，其未過宮也，汝愚數從容進諫，光宗出聞其語輒悟，入輒復疑。

translations.literal: Guangzong's illness arose from suspicion and fear; before he had visited the palace, Ruyu several times advanced remonstrance in an easy manner; when Guangzong went out and heard his words he would at once understand, but when he went in he would again grow suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzong's illness grew from suspicion and dread. Before he resumed visiting his father, Ruyu gently remonstrated with him many times. Guangzong would understand as he left, then doubt again once inside.

sentences.zh: 五年春，孝宗不豫，夏五月，疾日臻。

translations.literal: In spring of the fifth year Xiaozong was unwell; in the fifth month of summer the illness daily grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year five Xiaozong fell ill. By the fifth month his condition was worsening daily.

sentences.zh: 光宗御後殿，丞相率同列入，請上詣重華宮侍疾，從臣、臺諫繼入，閤門吏以故事止之，不退。

translations.literal: Guangzong held court in the rear hall; the chief minister led his colleagues in and asked the emperor to go to Chonghua Palace to attend the illness; attendant ministers and censor-remonstrators followed in; the gate officers by precedent tried to stop them but they would not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzong held court in the rear hall. The chief minister and his colleagues entered and begged him to attend Xiaozong at Chonghua Palace. Attendant ministers and censors followed. Gate officers tried to bar them by precedent, but they refused to leave.

sentences.zh: 光宗益疑，起入內。

translations.literal: Guangzong grew more suspicious, rose, and went within.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzong grew more suspicious, rose, and withdrew inside.

sentences.zh: 越二日，宰相又請對，光宗令知閤門事韓侂胄傳旨云：「宰執並出。」

translations.literal: After two days the chief ministers again requested audience; Guangzong had Director of the Palace Gate Han Tuozhou transmit the order: "Let all chief ministers go out."
translations.idiomatic: Two days later the chief ministers again asked for audience. Guangzong had palace gate director Han Tuozhou announce: "All chief ministers are to leave."

sentences.zh: 於是俱至浙江亭俟命。

translations.literal: Thereupon they all went to Zhejiang Pavilion to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: They all went to Zhejiang Pavilion to await further orders.

sentences.zh: 孝宗聞之憂甚，嗣秀王簡丞相傳孝宗意，令宰執復入。

translations.literal: Xiaozong heard of it and was deeply troubled; Prince of Xiuxiu sent a brief note to the chief minister conveying Xiaozong's wish and ordering the chief ministers to enter again.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong heard and was deeply troubled. Prince Xiuxiu sent the chief minister a note conveying Xiaozong's wish that the ministers return.

sentences.zh: 侂胄奏曰：「昨傳旨令宰執出殿門，今乃出都門。」

translations.literal: Tuozhou memorialized, "Yesterday the transmitted order told the chief ministers to leave the hall gate; now they have gone out the capital gate."
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou reported, "Yesterday's order sent the chief ministers out of the palace gate. Now they have left the capital gate altogether."

sentences.zh: 請自往宣押，汝愚等乃還第。

translations.literal: He asked to go himself to announce the recall; Ruyu and the others then returned to their residences.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to go announce a recall in person, and Ruyu and the others returned home.

sentences.zh: 六月丁酉，夜五鼓，重華大閹扣宰執私第，報孝宗崩，中書以聞，汝愚恐上疑，或不出視朝，持其劄不上。

translations.literal: On dingyou of the sixth month, at the fifth watch of the night, a great eunuch of Chonghua knocked at the chief ministers' private residences, reporting Xiaozong's death; the Secretariat reported it; Ruyu feared the emperor would be suspicious and perhaps not appear at court, and held the memorial without submitting it.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou of the sixth month, at the fifth watch, a senior Chonghua eunuch knocked at the ministers' doors with news of Xiaozong's death. The Secretariat reported it, but Ruyu feared suspicion would keep Guangzong from court and withheld the memorial.

sentences.zh: 次日，上視朝，汝愚以提舉重華宮關禮狀進，上乃許過北內，至日昃不出，宰相率百官詣重華宮發喪。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor held court; Ruyu advanced in his capacity as commissioner for Chonghua Palace rites the memorial of condolence, and the emperor then permitted a visit to the Northern Palace; until the sun declined he did not go out, and the chief minister led the hundred officials to Chonghua Palace to begin the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Guangzong held court. Ruyu submitted the condolence papers in his role as commissioner for Chonghua rites, and the emperor agreed to visit the Northern Palace—but did not emerge until after noon. The chief minister led the officials to Chonghua to begin the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，將成服，留正與汝愚議，介少傅吳琚請憲聖太后垂簾暫主喪事，憲聖不許。

translations.literal: On renyin, as they were about to put on the hemp mourning garments, Liu Zheng and Ruyu deliberated; Junior Mentor Wu Ju, acting as go-between, asked Empress Dowager Xiansheng to draw the curtain and temporarily preside over the mourning affairs; Xiansheng did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, as the hemp mourning garments were to be donned, Liu Zheng and Ruyu consulted. Junior mentor Wu Ju asked Empress Dowager Xiansheng to draw the curtain and temporarily oversee the funeral. She refused.

sentences.zh: 正等附奏曰：「臣等連日造南內請對，不獲。

translations.literal: Zheng and the others added a memorial, saying, "Your servants for successive days have gone to the Southern Palace to request audience and have not been granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng and the others added, "We have gone day after day to the Southern Palace seeking audience without success.

sentences.zh: 累上疏，不得報。

translations.literal: We have repeatedly submitted memorials and received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: We have submitted memorial after memorial without reply.

sentences.zh: 今當率百恭官請，若皇帝不出，百官相與慟哭于宮門，恐人情騷動，爲社稷憂。

translations.literal: Now we ought to lead the hundred officials in requesting; if the emperor does not come out, the hundred officials will together wail at the palace gate—we fear popular feeling will be disturbed and the altars of state endangered.
translations.idiomatic: We must now lead all officials in petition. If the emperor does not appear, the whole court will weep at the palace gate. We fear unrest among the people and peril to the realm.

sentences.zh: 乞太皇太后降旨，以皇帝有疾，蹔就宮中成服。

translations.literal: We beg the Grand Empress Dowager to issue an order that, because the emperor is ill, he may temporarily complete the mourning garments within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: We beg the Grand Empress Dowager to order that, because the emperor is ill, he may temporarily complete mourning within the palace.

sentences.zh: 然喪不可無主，祝文稱『孝子嗣皇帝』，宰臣不敢代行。

translations.literal: Yet mourning cannot be without a master; the prayer text reads 'filial son, succeeding emperor,' and the chief ministers dare not perform it in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Yet mourning cannot lack a chief mourner. The prayer names the 'filial son, succeeding emperor,' and we dare not perform it for him.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后，壽皇之母也，請攝行祭禮。」

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager is the mother of the Shouhuang Emperor; we ask that she act in his place to perform the sacrificial rites."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager is Xiaozong's mother. We ask her to preside at the rites in his stead."

sentences.zh: 蓋是時正、汝愚之請垂簾也，以國本係乎嘉王，欲因簾前奏陳宗社之計，使命出簾幃之間，事行廟堂之上，則體正言順，可無後艱。

translations.literal: In fact at this time what Zheng and Ruyu were requesting with the drawn curtain was that, since the foundation of the state depended on Prince Jia, they wished by memorial before the curtain to set forth plans for the altars of state, so that orders would issue from between curtain and screen and affairs would be carried out upon the temple hall—then the form would be correct, the words proper, and there would be no later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: In truth Zheng and Ruyu sought the drawn curtain because the succession hinged on Prince Jia. They hoped to lay state policy before the empress dowager at court, so orders would issue from behind the screen and business proceed in the open hall—proper in form and word, without later strife.

sentences.zh: 而吳琚素畏慎，且以后戚不欲與聞大計，此議竟格。

translations.literal: But Wu Ju was by nature timid and cautious, and moreover as a maternal relative of the empress did not wish to hear of great plans; this proposal in the end was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: But Wu Ju was timid by nature and, as the empress's kin, unwilling to hear of great designs. The plan was blocked.

sentences.zh: 丁未，宰臣已下，待對和寧門，不報，乃入奏云：「皇子嘉王仁孝夙成，宜早正儲位以安人心。」

translations.literal: On dingwei, the chief ministers and below waited for audience at the Gate of Harmonious Tranquility; receiving no reply, they entered and memorialized, saying, "Prince Jia is benevolent and filial and accomplished from youth; he should early be established as heir to settle people's hearts."
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei the chief ministers waited at the Gate of Harmonious Tranquility for audience without answer, then entered and said, "Prince Jia has shown filial virtue from youth. The heir apparent should be named early to steady the people's hearts."

sentences.zh: 又不報。

translations.literal: Again no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Again no reply.

sentences.zh: 越六日再請，御批云：「甚好。」

translations.literal: After six days they asked again; the imperial rescript read, "Very good."
translations.idiomatic: Six days later they asked again. The emperor's rescript read, "Very good."

sentences.zh: 明日，同擬旨以進，乞上親批付學士院降詔。

translations.literal: The next day they jointly drafted an order to advance and begged the emperor to personally annotate and deliver it to the Hanlin Academy to issue the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they jointly drafted an order and asked the emperor to annotate it personally and send it to the Hanlin Academy for promulgation.

sentences.zh: 是夕，御批付丞相云：「歷事歲久，念欲退閑。」

translations.literal: That evening an imperial rescript was delivered to the chief minister, reading, "I have served many years and think of retiring to leisure."
translations.idiomatic: That evening a rescript reached the chief minister: "I have served many years and wish to retire."

sentences.zh: 留正見之懼，因朝臨佯仆於庭，密爲去計。

translations.literal: When Liu Zheng saw it he was afraid; at the next court session he pretended to fall in the courtyard and secretly made plans to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zheng was terrified. At the next audience he feigned a fall in the courtyard and secretly planned his departure.

sentences.zh: 汝愚自度不得辭其責，念故事須坐甲以戒不虞，而殿帥郭杲莫有以腹心語者。

translations.literal: Ruyu reckoned he could not shirk his responsibility, reflected that precedent required sitting in armor to guard against the unexpected, yet Palace Commander Guo Gao had no one to speak to him from the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu knew he could not evade responsibility. Precedent required the guard to stand to arms against surprise, yet Palace Commander Guo Gao had no confidant he would trust.

sentences.zh: 會工部尚書趙彥逾至私第，語及國事，汝愚泣，彥逾亦泣，汝愚因微及與子意，彥逾喜。

translations.literal: It happened that Minister of Works Zhao Yanyu came to his private residence; when they spoke of state affairs Ruyu wept, Yanyu also wept, and Ruyu subtly touched on his intention regarding the heir; Yanyu was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Zhao Yanyu happened to visit his home. When they spoke of state affairs Ruyu wept, Yanyu wept too, and Ruyu hinted at his plan for the heir. Yanyu was delighted.

sentences.zh: 汝愚知彥逾善杲，因繆曰：「郭杲儻不同，奈何？」

translations.literal: Ruyu knew Yanyu was on good terms with Guo Gao and therefore said falsely, "If Guo Gao perchance does not agree, what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Yanyu was close to Guo Gao, Ruyu said disingenuously, "What if Guo Gao will not go along?"

sentences.zh: 彥逾曰：「某當任之。」

translations.literal: Yanyu said, "I will take responsibility for it."
translations.idiomatic: Yanyu said, "Leave that to me."

sentences.zh: 約明乃復命。

translations.literal: They agreed he would report back at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed he would return at dawn with word.

sentences.zh: 汝愚曰：「此大事已出諸口，豈容有所俟乎？」

translations.literal: Ruyu said, "This great matter has already passed our lips—how can we allow any waiting?"
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu said, "This great matter is already spoken—how can we wait?"

sentences.zh: 汝愚不敢入私室，退坐屏後，以待彥逾之至。

translations.literal: Ruyu dared not enter his private chamber, withdrew and sat behind the screen, waiting for Yanyu's arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu would not go to his inner room but sat behind the screen waiting for Yanyu.

sentences.zh: 有頃，彥逾至，議遂定。

translations.literal: Before long Yanyu arrived, and the plan was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yanyu returned and the plan was set.

sentences.zh: 明日，正以五更肩輿出城去，人心益搖，汝愚處之恬然。

translations.literal: The next day Liu Zheng at the fifth watch left the city in a shoulder carriage; popular feeling grew more unsettled, but Ruyu faced it with calm.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Liu Zheng left the city in a litter before dawn. Public anxiety grew, but Ruyu remained perfectly calm.

sentences.zh: 自吳琚之議不諧，汝愚與徐誼、葉適謀可以白意于慈福宮者，乃遣韓侂胄以內禪之意請於憲聖。

translations.literal: Since Wu Ju's proposal had not succeeded, Ruyu with Xu Yi and Ye Shi deliberated on who could convey their meaning to the Cifu Palace, and sent Han Tuozhou to request abdication in favor of the heir from Empress Dowager Xiansheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Ju's plan failed, Ruyu, Xu Yi, and Ye Shi looked for someone who could present their case at Cifu Palace and sent Han Tuozhou to ask Empress Dowager Xiansheng for an inner abdication.

sentences.zh: 侂胄因所善內侍張宗尹以奏，不獲命，明日往，又不獲命。

translations.literal: Tuozhou through the inner attendant Zhang Zongyin, whom he favored, presented the memorial but received no command; the next day he went again and again received no command.
translations.idiomatic: Through his friend the eunuch Zhang Zongyin he submitted the request but got no answer. He went again the next day and was refused again.

sentences.zh: 侂胄逡巡將退，重華宮提舉關禮見而問之，侂胄具述汝愚意。

translations.literal: Tuozhou hesitated and was about to withdraw when Guan Li, commissioner for Chonghua Palace rites, saw him and asked; Tuozhou fully related Ruyu's intention.
translations.idiomatic: As Tuozhou hesitated to leave, Guan Li, commissioner for Chonghua rites, saw him and asked what was wrong. Tuozhou explained Ruyu's plan in full.

sentences.zh: 禮令少俟，入見憲聖而泣。

translations.literal: Li told him to wait a little, entered to see Xiansheng, and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Li told him to wait, went in to see Xiansheng, and wept.

sentences.zh: 憲聖問故，禮曰：「聖人讀書萬卷，亦嘗見有如此時而保無亂者乎？」

translations.literal: Xiansheng asked the reason; Li said, "The sage has read ten thousand scrolls—has she ever seen a time like this and still kept the realm free of disorder?"
translations.idiomatic: When she asked why, Li said, "Your Majesty has read ten thousand books—has any age like this ever stayed free of chaos?"

sentences.zh: 憲聖曰：「此非汝所知。」

translations.literal: Xiansheng said, "This is not for you to know."
translations.idiomatic: She said, "That is not your affair to judge."

sentences.zh: 禮曰：「此事人人知之，今丞相已去，所賴者趙知院，旦夕亦去矣。」

translations.literal: Li said, "Everyone knows this matter; now the chief minister has gone, and what we rely on is Controller Zhao—he too will leave before long."
translations.idiomatic: Li replied, "Everyone knows it. The chief minister is already gone. All that remains is Controller Zhao—and he will be gone any day now."

sentences.zh: 言與淚俱。

translations.literal: His words came with tears.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke through his tears.

sentences.zh: 憲聖驚曰：「知院同姓，事體與他人異，乃亦去乎？」

translations.literal: Xiansheng said in alarm, "The controller shares our surname; his position differs from others—he too is leaving?"
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, she said, "The controller is of our own clan—his case is not like others'. He is leaving too?"

sentences.zh: 禮曰：「知院未去，非但以同姓故，以太皇太后爲可恃耳。

translations.literal: Li said, "The controller has not yet left not only because of shared surname, but because the Grand Empress Dowager could be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Li said, "He has not left yet only because he still trusts the Grand Empress Dowager—not merely because he shares your surname.

sentences.zh: 今定大計而不獲命，勢不得不去，將如天下何？

translations.literal: Now the great plan is settled yet no command is granted; the situation forces him to leave—what will become of the realm?
translations.idiomatic: Now the great decision is made but you will not approve it. He has no choice but to go. What then becomes of the realm?

sentences.zh: 願聖人三思。」

translations.literal: I beg the sage to think thrice."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to think again."

sentences.zh: 憲聖問侂胄安在，禮曰：「臣已留其俟命。」

translations.literal: Xiansheng asked where Tuozhou was; Li said, "Your servant has kept him waiting for orders."
translations.idiomatic: She asked where Tuozhou was. Li said, "I have kept him waiting outside for your word."

sentences.zh: 憲聖曰：「事順則可，令諭好爲之。」

translations.literal: Xiansheng said, "If the affair accords with principle it may proceed; tell him to carry it out well."
translations.idiomatic: She said, "If the matter is proper, let it proceed. Tell him to see it done well."

sentences.zh: 禮報侂胄，且云：「來早太皇太后于壽皇梓宮前垂簾引執政。」

translations.literal: Li reported to Tuozhou and also said, "Tomorrow morning the Grand Empress Dowager will draw the curtain before the Shouhuang coffin and summon the chief ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Li reported to Tuozhou and added, "Tomorrow morning the Grand Empress Dowager will draw the curtain before Xiaozong's coffin and receive the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 侂胄復命，汝愚始以其事語陳騤、余端禮，使郭杲及步帥閻仲夜以兵衛南北內，禮使其姻黨宣贊舍人傅昌朝密制黃袍。

translations.literal: Tuozhou returned with the reply; Ruyu then told Chen Tuan and Yu Duanli of the affair, had Guo Gao and infantry commander Yan Zhongye guard the Northern and Southern palaces with troops, and Li had his affinal kin, palace announcer Fu Changchao, secretly make the yellow robe.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou brought word back. Ruyu then told Chen Tuan and Yu Duanli, had Guo Gao and infantry commander Yan Zhongye post troops at both palaces, and Li had his kinsman, palace announcer Fu Changchao, secretly make the imperial yellow robe.

sentences.zh: 是日，嘉王謁告不入臨，汝愚曰：「禫祭重事，王不可不出。」

translations.literal: That day Prince Jia requested leave and did not attend the mourning vigil; Ruyu said, "The chan sacrifice is a weighty matter—the prince cannot stay away."
translations.idiomatic: That day Prince Jia asked to be excused from the mourning vigil. Ruyu said, "The chan sacrifice is a grave affair. The prince must attend."

sentences.zh: 翌日，禫祭，群臣入，王亦入。

translations.literal: The next day at the chan sacrifice the hundred officials entered, and the prince entered as well.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, at the chan rites, the officials entered—and the prince entered too.

sentences.zh: 汝愚率百官詣大行前，憲聖垂簾，汝愚率同列再拜，奏：「皇帝疾，未能執喪，臣等乞立皇子嘉王爲太子，以繫人心。

translations.literal: Ruyu led the hundred officials before the late emperor; Xiansheng drew the curtain. Ruyu led his colleagues in double obeisance and memorialized, "The emperor is ill and unable to perform mourning; your servants beg to establish Prince Jia as heir apparent to bind people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu led the officials before the late emperor's bier while Xiansheng drew the curtain. He and his colleagues bowed twice and said, "The emperor is ill and cannot mourn. We beg that Prince Jia be made heir apparent to steady the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 皇帝批出有『甚好』二字，繼有『念欲退閑』之語，取太皇太后處分。」

translations.literal: The emperor's rescript bore the two characters 'very good,' followed by words 'thinking of retiring to leisure'; we seek the Grand Empress Dowager's disposition."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's rescript said 'very good,' then spoke of wishing to retire. We ask the Grand Empress Dowager to decide."

sentences.zh: 憲聖曰：「既有御筆，相公當奉行。」

translations.literal: Xiansheng said, "Since there is an imperial brushnote, the chief minister should carry it out."
translations.idiomatic: She said, "Since there is an imperial note, the chief minister should obey it."

sentences.zh: 汝愚曰：「茲事重大，播之天下，書之史冊，須議一指揮。」

translations.literal: Ruyu said, "This matter is weighty—it will be broadcast to the realm and written in the historical records; an order must be deliberated."
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu said, "This is too grave to leave informal. It will be known throughout the realm and recorded in history. We need a formal order."

sentences.zh: 憲聖允諾。

translations.literal: Xiansheng consented.
translations.idiomatic: She agreed.

sentences.zh: 汝愚袖出所擬太皇太后指揮以進，云：「皇帝以疾至今未能執喪，曾有御筆，欲自退閑。

translations.literal: Ruyu drew from his sleeve the draft Grand Empress Dowager order he had prepared and advanced it, saying, "The emperor, because of illness to this day unable to perform mourning, once had an imperial brushnote wishing to retire to leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu produced from his sleeve the draft order he had prepared: "Because of illness the emperor has been unable to mourn. He once wrote that he wished to retire.

sentences.zh: 皇子嘉王擴可即皇帝位，尊皇帝爲太上皇帝，皇后爲太上皇后。」

translations.literal: Prince Jia Kuo may immediately take the imperial throne; let the emperor be honored as Retired Emperor and the empress as Retired Empress."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jia Kuo shall immediately ascend the throne. The emperor shall be honored as Retired Emperor and the empress as Retired Empress."

sentences.zh: 憲聖覽畢曰：「甚善。」

translations.literal: When Xiansheng had read it through she said, "Very good."
translations.idiomatic: After reading it she said, "Excellent."

sentences.zh: 汝愚奏：「自今臣等有合奏事，當取嗣君處分。

translations.literal: Ruyu memorialized, "From now on when your servants have matters requiring memorial, we should take disposition from the succeeding ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu added, "From now on our memorials should go to the new emperor.

sentences.zh: 然恐兩宮父子間有難處者，須煩太皇太后主張。」

translations.literal: Yet we fear there may be difficult points between the two palaces, father and son, and must trouble the Grand Empress Dowager to decide."
translations.idiomatic: But we fear difficulties between father and son at the two palaces and ask the Grand Empress Dowager to preside."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「上皇疾未平，驟聞此事，不無驚疑，乞令都知楊舜卿提舉本宮，任其責。」

translations.literal: He further memorialized, "The Retired Emperor's illness is not yet settled; hearing this matter suddenly, he cannot be without alarm and doubt. We beg that Director Yang Shunqing be ordered to oversee the Retired Emperor's palace and bear the responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: He also asked, "The Retired Emperor is still ill. This news may alarm him. Let Director Yang Shunqing oversee his palace and bear full responsibility."

sentences.zh: 遂召舜卿至簾前，面喻之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shunqing was summoned before the curtain and instructed face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Shunqing was summoned before the curtain and instructed in person.

sentences.zh: 憲聖乃命皇子即位，皇子固辭曰：「恐負不孝名。」

translations.literal: Xiansheng then ordered the prince to take the throne; the prince firmly declined, saying, "I fear bearing the name of unfilial son."
translations.idiomatic: Xiansheng then ordered the prince to ascend. He firmly refused: "I fear the charge of unfiliality."

sentences.zh: 汝愚奏：「天子當以安社稷、定國家爲孝。

translations.literal: Ruyu memorialized, "The Son of Heaven should take securing the altars of state and settling the realm as filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu said, "For a Son of Heaven, filial piety means securing the altars and settling the realm.

sentences.zh: 今中外人人憂亂，萬一變生，置太上皇何地？」

translations.literal: Now within and without everyone fears disorder; if by chance change arises, where will the Retired Emperor be placed?"
translations.idiomatic: Within and without the court everyone fears chaos. If trouble breaks out, what becomes of the Retired Emperor?"

sentences.zh: 衆扶入素幄，披黃袍，方卻立未坐，汝愚率同列再拜。

translations.literal: The crowd helped him into the plain canopy, draped the yellow robe on him; he had just stepped back and not yet sat when Ruyu led his colleagues in double obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: They helped him into the plain canopy and draped the yellow robe on him. He had barely stepped back when Ruyu and his colleagues bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 寧宗詣几筵殿，哭盡哀。

translations.literal: Ningzong went to the Hall of the Spirit Table and wept to the full of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzong went to the spirit hall and wept his fill.

sentences.zh: 須臾，立仗訖，催百官班。

translations.literal: Before long the guard formation was complete and the hundred officials were urged to form ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly the guard was drawn up and the officials were called to ranks.

sentences.zh: 帝衰服出就重華殿東廡素幄立，內侍扶掖乃坐。

translations.literal: The emperor in hemp mourning came out and took his place standing in the plain canopy of the eastern corridor of Chonghua Hall; inner attendants supported him before he could sit.
translations.idiomatic: In hemp mourning the emperor came out to the plain canopy in Chonghua's east corridor. Attendants had to support him before he could sit.

sentences.zh: 百官起居訖，行禫祭禮。

translations.literal: When the hundred officials had finished the greeting ceremony, the chan sacrifice rites were performed.
translations.idiomatic: After the officials had paid their respects, the chan rites were performed.

sentences.zh: 汝愚即喪次，召還留正長百僚，命朱熹待制經筵，悉收召士君子之在外者。

translations.literal: Ruyu at once at the mourning site recalled Liu Zheng to head the hundred officials, appointed Zhu Xi as academician attendant on the classics colloquium, and altogether recalled gentlemen of worth who were outside.
translations.idiomatic: At the mourning site Ruyu recalled Liu Zheng to head the officials, appointed Zhu Xi to the classics colloquium, and brought back worthy men who had been abroad.

sentences.zh: 侍御史張叔椿請議正棄國之罰，汝愚爲遷叔椿官。

translations.literal: Attendant censor Zhang Shuchun asked that Liu Zheng's punishment for abandoning the state be deliberated; Ruyu had Shuchun's office changed upward for him.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant censor Zhang Shuchun asked that Liu Zheng be punished for deserting his post. Ruyu promoted Shuchun instead.

sentences.zh: 是月，上命汝愚兼權參知政事。

translations.literal: That month the emperor ordered Ruyu to concurrently act as participant in governance.
translations.idiomatic: That month the emperor named Ruyu acting vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 留正至，汝愚乞免兼職，乃除特進、右丞相。

translations.literal: When Liu Zheng arrived, Ruyu begged to be relieved of the concurrent post and was appointed specially advanced and right chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zheng returned, Ruyu asked to give up the concurrent post and was made specially advanced right chief minister.

sentences.zh: 汝愚辭不拜，曰：「同姓之卿，不幸處君臣之變，敢言功乎？」

translations.literal: Ruyu declined and did not accept, saying, "A minister of the same surname, unhappily placed in the change between ruler and subject—how dare I speak of merit?"
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu refused to accept, saying, "A kinsman minister caught in this change between sovereign and subject—how dare I claim merit?"

sentences.zh: 乃命以特進爲樞密使，汝愚又辭特進。

translations.literal: He was then ordered as specially advanced to be controller of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Ruyu again declined the specially advanced rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to be Military Affairs controller with specially advanced rank. Ruyu declined the rank.

sentences.zh: 孝宗將攢，汝愚議攢宮非永制，欲改卜山陵，與留正議不合。

translations.literal: As Xiaozong was about to be placed in the temporary palace, Ruyu argued that the temporary palace was not a permanent institution and wished to choose a new site for the mountain tomb; he did not agree with Liu Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: As Xiaozong was to be placed in the temporary palace, Ruyu argued that this was not permanent and wanted a new mountain tomb site. He and Liu Zheng disagreed.

sentences.zh: 侂胄因而間之，出正判建康，命汝愚爲光祿大夫、右丞相。

translations.literal: Tuozhou thereby drove a wedge between them, sent Zheng out as prefect of Jiankang, and appointed Ruyu as Grandee for Splendid Happiness and right chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou drove a wedge between them, sent Zheng to Jiankang, and made Ruyu Grandee for Splendid Happiness and right chief minister.

sentences.zh: 汝愚力辭至再三，不許。

translations.literal: Ruyu strongly declined again and again; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu refused again and again but was not allowed to decline.

sentences.zh: 汝愚本倚正共事，怒侂胄不以告，及來謁，故不見，侂胄慚忿。

translations.literal: Ruyu had originally relied on Zheng to work together; he was angry that Tuozhou had not informed him, and when Tuozhou came to call, deliberately did not see him; Tuozhou was ashamed and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu had counted on working with Zheng and was angry that Tuozhou had not told him. When Tuozhou came to call, he refused to see him. Tuozhou was humiliated and furious.

sentences.zh: 簽書樞密羅點曰：「公誤矣。」

translations.literal: Signatory of Military Affairs Luo Dian said, "My lord is mistaken."
translations.idiomatic: Military Affairs signatory Luo Dian said, "You are mistaken, my lord."

sentences.zh: 汝愚亦悟，復見之。

translations.literal: Ruyu also understood and received him again.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu saw his error and received Tuozhou again.

sentences.zh: 侂胄終不懌，自以有定策功，且依託肺腑，出入宮掖，居中用事。

translations.literal: Tuozhou in the end was not pleased; he considered himself to have merit in settling the policy, and moreover relied on being a close kin by marriage, going in and out of the palace women's quarters, holding power at the center.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou remained displeased. He credited himself with settling the succession, relied on his marriage tie to the imperial clan, moved freely in the inner palace, and wielded power at court.

sentences.zh: 朱熹進對，以爲言，又約吏部侍郎彭龜年同劾之，未果。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi entered for audience and spoke on this; he also arranged with vice-minister of Personnel Peng Guinian to impeach Tuozhou together, but it did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi remonstrated at audience and arranged with vice-minister Peng Guinian to impeach Tuozhou together, but failed.

sentences.zh: 熹白汝愚，當以厚賞酬勞，勿使預政，而汝愚謂其易制不爲慮。

translations.literal: Xi told Ruyu he should reward him generously and not let him participate in government, but Ruyu thought him easy to control and did not worry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi told Ruyu to reward Tuozhou richly and keep him from office. Ruyu thought him easy to control and paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 侂胄恃功，爲汝愚所抑，日夜謀引其黨爲臺諫，以擯汝愚。

translations.literal: Tuozhou relied on his merit and, being restrained by Ruyu, day and night plotted to bring in his faction as censors and remonstrators to drive Ruyu out.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou, checked by Ruyu, relied on his merit and plotted day and night to install his men as censors and drive Ruyu out.

sentences.zh: 汝愚爲人疏，不虞其姦。

translations.literal: Ruyu by nature was open and did not guard against his treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu was open by nature and did not foresee his treachery.

sentences.zh: 趙彥逾以嘗達意于郭杲，事定，冀汝愚引與同列，至是除四川制置，意不愜，與侂胄合謀。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanyu, because he had once conveyed the intention to Guo Gao, when the affair was settled hoped Ruyu would bring him into the chief ministers' ranks; now he was appointed Sichuan commissioner, was not satisfied, and joined in Tuozhou's plot.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanyu, who had once conveyed the plan to Guo Gao, hoped Ruyu would bring him into the chief ministers' circle. Instead he was sent to Sichuan as commissioner, was dissatisfied, and joined Tuozhou's plot.

sentences.zh: 陛辭日，盡疏當時賢者姓名，指爲汝愚之黨，上意不能無疑。

translations.literal: On his farewell audience day he fully listed the names of worthy men of the time, pointing to them as Ruyu's faction; the emperor's mind could not be without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience he listed every worthy man of the day as Ruyu's partisan. The emperor could not help but doubt.

sentences.zh: 汝愚請令近臣舉御史，侂胄密諭中司，令薦所厚大理寺簿劉德秀，內批擢德秀爲察官，其黨牽聯以進，言路遂皆侂胄之人。

translations.literal: Ruyu asked that close ministers recommend censors; Tuozhou secretly instructed the chief supervising secretary to recommend his favorite, Grand Court clerk Liu Dexiu; an inner rescript promoted Dexiu to investigating officer; his faction advanced one another, and the remonstrance route thus became entirely Tuozhou's men.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu asked close ministers to recommend censors. Tuozhou secretly told the chief supervising secretary to nominate his protégé Liu Dexiu of the Grand Court. An inner rescript made Dexiu investigating censor, and Tuozhou's men took over the remonstrance offices.

sentences.zh: 會黃裳、羅點卒，侂胄又擢其黨京鏜代點，汝愚始孤，天子益無所倚信。

translations.literal: When Huang Shang and Luo Dian died, Tuozhou again promoted his faction member Jing Tang to replace Dian; Ruyu was then isolated, and the Son of Heaven increasingly had no one to rely on and trust.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Shang and Luo Dian died, Tuozhou installed his man Jing Tang in Luo's place. Ruyu was isolated, and the emperor had no one left to trust.

sentences.zh: 於是中書舍人陳傅良、監察御史吳獵、起居郎劉光祖各先後斥去，群憸和附，疾正士如仇讎，而衣冠之禍始矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Secretariat drafter Chen Fuliang, investigating censor Wu Lie, and diarist Liu Guangzu were each in turn driven out; the crowd of sycophants joined in flattery, hated upright gentlemen like mortal enemies, and the calamity of the scholar-official class began.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat drafter Chen Fuliang, censor Wu Lie, and diarist Liu Guangzu were driven out in turn. Sycophants flocked to Tuozhou and hated upright men like mortal foes. The persecution of the scholar-official class had begun.

sentences.zh: 侂胄欲逐汝愚而難其名，或教之曰：「彼宗姓，誣以謀危社稷，則一網無遺。」

translations.literal: Tuozhou wished to drive Ruyu out but found it hard to name a charge; someone taught him, saying, "He is of the imperial clan—slander him with plotting to endanger the altars of state, and not one will be left in the net."
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou wanted to oust Ruyu but lacked a charge. Someone advised him, "He is of the imperial clan. Accuse him of plotting against the realm and you can sweep up the whole faction."

sentences.zh: 侂胄然之，擢其黨將作監李沐爲正言。

translations.literal: Tuozhou approved this and promoted his faction member Li Mu of the Directorate of Palace Buildings to chief remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou agreed and made his man Li Mu of the Directorate of Palace Buildings chief remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 沐，彥穎之子也，嘗求節度使于汝愚不得，奏：「汝愚以同姓居相位，將不利於社稷，乞罷其政。」

translations.literal: Mu was the son of Yan Ying; he had once asked Ruyu for a military commissioner post and not obtained it. He memorialized, "Ruyu, as one of the same surname holding the chief minister's post, will be unfavorable to the altars of state; I beg that his government be ended."
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu was Yan Ying's son. He had once asked Ruyu for a military commission and been refused. He memorialized, "Ruyu holds the chief ministership as an imperial kinsman and will harm the realm. I beg that he be removed from office."

sentences.zh: 汝愚出浙江亭待罪，遂罷右相，除觀文殿學士、知福州。

translations.literal: Ruyu went out to Zhejiang Pavilion to await punishment, was then dismissed as right chief minister, and appointed academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture and prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu went to Zhejiang Pavilion to await punishment. He was dismissed as right chief minister and made academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture and prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 臺臣合詞乞寢出守之命，遂以大學士提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: Censors together in one voice begged to suspend the order sending him out to govern, and he was then made grand academician and commissioner of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Censors united in asking that the prefectural appointment be withdrawn. He was made grand academician and commissioner of Dongxiao Palace instead.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒李祥言：「去歲國遭大戚，中外洶洶，留正棄相位而去，官僚幾欲解散，軍民皆將爲亂，兩宮隔絕，國喪無主。

translations.literal: Libationer of the National University Li Xiang said, "Last year the state met great grief; within and without there was uproar. Liu Zheng abandoned the chief minister's post and left; the bureaucracy nearly dissolved; soldiers and civilians were all about to riot; the two palaces were cut off from each other; the state mourning had no master.
translations.idiomatic: National University libationer Li Xiang said, "Last year the state suffered a great bereavement. Within and without there was uproar. Liu Zheng abandoned office. The bureaucracy nearly collapsed. Soldiers and civilians were on the verge of riot. The two palaces were estranged and mourning had no chief.

sentences.zh: 汝愚以樞臣獨不避殞身滅族之禍，奉太皇太后命，翊陛下以登九五，勳勞著於社稷，精忠貫於天地，乃卒受黯黮而去，天下後世其謂何？」

translations.literal: Ruyu alone as controller did not avoid the calamity of perishing body and extinguished clan, received the Grand Empress Dowager's command, and assisted Your Majesty to ascend the throne; his merit was manifest on the altars of state, his pure loyalty penetrated heaven and earth—yet in the end he received obscurity and dismissal. What will the realm and posterity say?"
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu alone, as Military Affairs controller, risked death and the destruction of his clan, obeyed the Grand Empress Dowager, and helped Your Majesty to the throne. His merit stands on the altars, his loyalty reaches heaven and earth—yet he is cast out in disgrace. What will the world say?"

sentences.zh: 博士楊簡亦以爲言。

translations.literal: Erudite Yang Jian also spoke to the same effect.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Yang Jian spoke similarly.

sentences.zh: 李沐劾祥、簡，罷之。

translations.literal: Li Mu impeached Xiang and Jian and had them dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu impeached Xiang and Jian and had them removed.

sentences.zh: 太府丞呂祖儉亦上書訴汝愚之忠，詔祖儉朋比罔上，送韶州安置。

translations.literal: Assistant director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury Lü Zujian also submitted a memorial pleading Ruyu's loyalty; an edict said Zujian had formed factions and deceived the ruler, and he was sent to Shaozhou for resettlement.
translations.idiomatic: Treasury assistant director Lü Zujian also memorialized in Ruyu's defense. An edict called him a faction-monger deceiving the throne and sent him to Shaozhou in exile.

sentences.zh: 太學生楊宏中、周端朝、張衜、林仲麟、蔣傅、徐範等伏闕言：「去歲人情驚疑，變在朝夕。

translations.literal: National University students Yang Hongzhong, Zhou Duanzhao, Zhang Dao, Lin Zhonglin, Jiang Fu, Xu Fan, and others prostrated themselves at the palace gate, saying, "Last year popular feeling was alarmed and doubtful; change was imminent morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: National University students Yang Hongzhong, Zhou Duanzhao, Zhang Dao, Lin Zhonglin, Jiang Fu, Xu Fan, and others knelt at the palace gate and said, "Last year the people were terrified. Disaster was imminent day and night.

sentences.zh: 當時假非汝愚出死力，定大議，雖百李沐，罔知攸濟。

translations.literal: At that time, if not for Ruyu exerting deadly effort and settling the great decision, even a hundred Li Mus would not know how to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Had Ruyu not risked his life to settle the succession, not even a hundred Li Mus could have saved the day.

sentences.zh: 當國家多難，汝愚位樞府，本兵柄，指揮操縱，何向不可，不以此時爲利，今上下安恬，乃獨有異志乎？」

translations.literal: When the state had many difficulties, Ruyu held the Bureau of Military Affairs and commanded military power—directing and manipulating, what could he not do? He did not take advantage at that time; now above and below are calm and at ease—does he alone harbor different intentions?"
translations.idiomatic: In the crisis Ruyu held Military Affairs and commanded the army. He could have taken any advantage then. He did not. Now that court and country are calm, does he alone harbor treason?"

sentences.zh: 書上，悉送五百里外羈管。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, all were sent for detention and control five hundred li away.
translations.idiomatic: Their memorial was received and all were exiled five hundred li away under guard.

sentences.zh: 汝愚學務有用，常以司馬光、富弼、韓琦、范仲淹自期。

translations.literal: Ruyu in learning strove for practical use and often set himself the standard of Sima Guang, Fu Bi, Han Qi, and Fan Zhongyan.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu pursued learning for practical use and measured himself against Sima Guang, Fu Bi, Han Qi, and Fan Zhongyan.

sentences.zh: 凡平昔所聞于師友，如張栻、朱熹、呂祖謙、汪應辰、王十朋、胡銓、李燾、林光朝之言，欲次第行之，未果。

translations.literal: All he had heard in ordinary times from teachers and friends—such as the words of Zhang Shi, Zhu Xi, Lü Zuqian, Wang Yingchen, Wang Shipeng, Hu Quan, Li Tao, and Lin Guangchao—he wished to carry out in order, but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: He hoped to put into practice in turn the teachings of Zhang Shi, Zhu Xi, Lü Zuqian, Wang Yingchen, Wang Shipeng, Hu Quan, Li Tao, Lin Guangchao, and others—but never succeeded.

sentences.zh: 所著詩文十五卷、《太祖實錄舉要》若干卷、《類宋朝諸臣奏議》三百卷。

translations.literal: His writings included fifteen juan of poetry and prose, several juan of Essentials from the Veritable Records of Taizu, and three hundred juan of Classified Memorials and Opinions of Song Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote fifteen juan of poetry and prose, several juan of Essentials from Taizu's Veritable Records, and three hundred juan of Classified Memorials of Song Ministers.

sentences.zh: 汝愚聚族而居，門內三千指，所得廩給悉分與之，菜羹疏食，恩意均洽，人無間言。

translations.literal: Ruyu gathered the clan to live together; within the gates were three thousand mouths; all stipends received he entirely divided among them—vegetable broth and plain food, kindness and favor equally extended, and no one had words of division.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu housed his whole clan—three thousand mouths under one roof. He divided every stipend among them, lived on vegetables and plain fare, treated all alike, and no one complained.

sentences.zh: 自奉養甚薄，爲夕郎時，大冬衣布裘，至爲相亦然。

translations.literal: His own maintenance was very meager; when he was a Secretariat reviewer, in deep winter he wore cloth fur, and even as chief minister it was the same.
translations.idiomatic: He lived very frugally. As a Secretariat reviewer he wore cloth fur even in deep winter, and did the same as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 汝愚既歿，黨禁寖解，旋復資政殿學士、太中大夫，已而贈少保。

translations.literal: After Ruyu died, the faction ban gradually eased; he was soon restored as academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and Grandee of Palace Attendance, and later posthumously given the title of Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: After Ruyu's death the faction ban gradually eased. He was restored as academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and Grandee of Palace Attendance, then posthumously made Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 侂胄誅，盡復元官，賜諡「忠定」，贈太師，追封沂國公。

translations.literal: When Tuozhou was executed, all his original offices were fully restored; he was given the posthumous title Loyal and Settled, posthumously made Grand Preceptor, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yi retroactively.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuozhou was executed, all Ruyu's offices were restored. He was given the posthumous name Loyal and Settled, made Grand Preceptor, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yi.

sentences.zh: 理宗詔配享寧宗廟庭，追封福王，其後進封周王。

translations.literal: Lizong decreed his enshrinement in Ningzong's temple court, enfeoffed him retroactively as Prince of Fu, and later advanced the enfeoffment to Prince of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lizong ordered him enshrined in Ningzong's temple, enfeoffed him as Prince of Fu, and later advanced the title to Prince of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 子九人，崇憲，其長子也。

translations.literal: He had nine sons; Chongxian was the eldest.
translations.idiomatic: He had nine sons. Chongxian was the eldest.

sentences.zh: 子 崇憲

translations.literal: Son: Chongxian
translations.idiomatic: Son: Chongxian

sentences.zh: 崇憲，字履常，淳熙八年以取應對策第一，時汝愚侍立殿上，降，再拜以謝。

translations.literal: Chongxian, courtesy name Lüchang, in the eighth year of Chunxi took first place in the special response examination; at the time Ruyu attended standing in the hall; he descended and bowed twice in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxian, styled Lüchang, took first place in the special response examination in Chunxi year 8. Ruyu was attending in the hall. He came down and bowed twice in thanks.

sentences.zh: 孝宗顧近臣曰：「汝愚年幾何？

translations.literal: Xiaozong turned to close ministers and said, "How old is Ruyu?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong turned to his close ministers and said, "How old is Ruyu?

sentences.zh: 已有子如此。」

translations.literal: He already has a son like this."
translations.idiomatic: To have a son like this already!"

sentences.zh: 越三年，復以進士對策，擢甲科。

translations.literal: Three years later he again took the jinshi policy response and was selected in the top grade.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he took the jinshi examination and was placed in the top grade.

sentences.zh: 上謂執政曰：「此汝愚子，豈即前科取應第一人者耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to the chief ministers, "This is Ruyu's son—is he not the one who was first in the special response examination of the previous session?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to the chief ministers, "This is Ruyu's son—isn't he the boy who came first in the special examination three years ago?"

sentences.zh: 崇憲初仕爲保義郎、監饒州贍軍酒庫，換從事郎、撫州軍事推官。

translations.literal: Chongxian's first offices were Gentleman for Preserving Righteousness and supervisor of the Raozhou army provision wine depot; he exchanged to staff officer and military judicial officer of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxian's first posts were Gentleman for Preserving Righteousness and supervisor of the Raozhou army provision wine depot, then staff officer and military judicial officer of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 汝愚帥蜀，辟書寫機宜文字，改江西轉運司幹辦公事，監西京中嶽廟。

translations.literal: When Ruyu commanded Shu, he recruited him as drafting officer for confidential matters; he was changed to executive clerk of the Jiangxi transport commission and supervisor of the Central Peak temple of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruyu commanded Sichuan he recruited him as confidential drafting officer, then made him executive clerk on the Jiangxi transport commission and supervisor of the Central Peak temple.

sentences.zh: 汝愚既貶死，海內憤鬱，崇憲闔門自處。

translations.literal: After Ruyu was demoted and died, within the seas there was anger and grief; Chongxian shut his gates and kept to himself.
translations.idiomatic: After Ruyu was disgraced and died, the empire seethed with anger. Chongxian shut his doors and lived in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 居數年，復汝愚故官職，多勸以仕。

translations.literal: After several years Ruyu's former offices were restored; many urged him to take office.
translations.idiomatic: After several years Ruyu's offices were restored and many urged Chongxian to serve again.

sentences.zh: 改奉議郎、知南昌縣事，奉行荒政，所活甚衆。

translations.literal: He was changed to Gentleman for Advising the Court and magistrate of Nanchang County; he carried out famine relief policy and the number he saved was very great.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Gentleman for Advising the Court and magistrate of Nanchang County, where he carried out famine relief and saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 升籍田令，制曰：「爾先人有功王室，中更讒毀，思其功而錄其子，國之典也。」

translations.literal: He was promoted to magistrate of the state fields; the edict read, "Your forebear had merit for the royal house, in the middle suffered slander and ruin—to recall his merit and record his son is the state's canon."
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to magistrate of the state fields. The edict read, "Your father served the throne with merit, then suffered slander. To honor his service by advancing his son is the state's custom."

sentences.zh: 崇憲拜命感泣，陳疏力辭，以爲「先臣之冤未悉昭白，而其孤先被寵光，非公朝所以勸忠孝、厲廉恥之意」。

translations.literal: Chongxian received the appointment with moved tears, submitted a memorial strongly declining, holding that "my late father's injustice is not yet fully cleared, yet his orphan is first favored with glory—this is not the court's intent to encourage loyalty and filial piety and sharpen integrity and shame."
translations.idiomatic: Chongxian accepted the appointment in tears but memorialized to decline, saying, "My father's wrong is not yet fully cleared, yet his orphan is favored first. This is not how the court should encourage loyalty, filial piety, and integrity."

sentences.zh: 俄改監行在都進奏院，復引陳瓘論司馬光、呂公著復官事申言之，乞以所陳下三省集議：「若先臣心跡有一如言者所論，即近日恩典皆爲冒濫，先臣復官賜諡，與臣新命，俱合追寢。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to supervisor of the capital memorial transmission office; he again cited Chen Guan's discussion of the restoration of offices for Sima Guang and Lü Gongzhu and stated it anew, begging that what he stated be sent down to the three departments for collective deliberation: "If my late father's conduct in heart and deed has any point like what the speakers argued, then the recent favors are all presumptuous excess, my late father's restored office and granted posthumous title, and my new appointment, should all be pursued and withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made supervisor of the capital memorial transmission office. He cited Chen Guan's memorial on restoring Sima Guang and Lü Gongzhu and asked the three departments to deliberate: "If my father's conduct was truly as his accusers claimed, then recent favors were undeserved, my father's restoration and posthumous title should be revoked, and my new appointment withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 如公論果謂誣衊，乞昭示中外，使先臣之讒謗既辨，忠節自明，而憲聖慈烈皇后擁佑之功德益顯。

translations.literal: If public opinion truly holds it was slander and defamation, I beg that it be made clear within and without, so that my late father's calumny is already distinguished, loyal integrity is self-evident, and the merit of Empress Dowager Xiansheng Cilie in supporting and protecting is the more manifest.
translations.idiomatic: If public opinion holds he was slandered, I beg that this be proclaimed throughout the realm, so my father's name is cleared, his loyalty made plain, and the merit of Empress Dowager Xiansheng Cilie in protecting the succession stands forth the more clearly.

sentences.zh: 然後申飭史官、改正誣史，垂萬世之公。」

translations.literal: Only then order the historiographers and correct the slanderous history, leaving fairness for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: Then order the historiographers to correct the slanderous record and leave justice to ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 又請正趙師召妄貢封章之罪，究蔡璉與大臣爲仇之姦，毀龔頤正《續稽古錄》之妄。

translations.literal: He also asked to rectify Zhao Shizhao's crime in presumptuously submitting sealed memorials, investigate Cai Lian's treachery in making enemies of chief ministers, and condemn the error of Gong Yizheng's Continued Record of Examining Antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that Zhao Shizhao be punished for presumptuous memorials, Cai Lian investigated for feuding with chief ministers, and Gong Yizheng's Continued Record of Examining Antiquity condemned as false.

sentences.zh: 詔兩省史官考訂以聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the historiographers of the two departments to examine and revise and report.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the historiographers of both departments to investigate and report.

sentences.zh: 已而吏部尚書兼修國史樓鑰等請施行如章，從之。

translations.literal: Before long Minister of Personnel and concurrent compiler of the national history Lou Yue and others asked that it be carried out as memorialized, and it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Minister of Personnel and national history compiler Lou Yue and others asked that Chongxian's requests be implemented as written, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 及誣史未正，復進言，其略謂：「前日史官徒以權臣風旨，刊舊史、焚元稿，略無留難。

translations.literal: When the slanderous history had not yet been corrected, he again advanced words, in summary saying, "Formerly the historiographers merely followed the powerful minister's intent, revised the old history, burned the original drafts, and had hardly any difficulty in doing so.
translations.idiomatic: When the falsified record had still not been corrected, he memorialized again in summary: "Earlier the historiographers simply followed a powerful minister's wishes, revised the old history, and burned the originals without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 今詔旨再三，莫有慨然奮直筆者，何小人敢於爲惡，而謂之君子者顧不能勇於爲善耶？」

translations.literal: Now imperial orders have come again and again, yet none stir themselves to wield the upright brush—why do petty men dare to do evil, while those called gentlemen cannot boldly do good?"
translations.idiomatic: Now edicts have come again and again, yet no one stirs to write the truth with an upright brush. Why do petty men dare do evil while so-called gentlemen cannot boldly do good?"

sentences.zh: 聞者愧之。

translations.literal: Those who heard were ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard were shamed.

sentences.zh: 其後玉牒、日曆所卒以《重修龍飛事實》進呈，因崇憲請也。

translations.literal: Afterward the Jade Register and Calendar Office at last presented the Revised Record of the Dragon's Ascent, because of Chongxian's request.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Jade Register and Calendar Office presented the Revised Record of the Dragon's Ascent at Chongxian's request.

sentences.zh: 未幾，贈汝愚太師，封沂國公，擢崇憲軍器監丞，改太府監丞，遷祕書郎，辭，弗許。

translations.literal: Before long Ruyu was posthumously given Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed as Duke of Yi, and Chongxian was promoted to assistant director of the Directorate of Armaments, changed to assistant director of the Imperial Treasury, moved to secretary, declined, and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Ruyu was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Duke of Yi. Chongxian was promoted to assistant director of the Directorate of Armaments, then the Imperial Treasury, then made secretary. He declined but was not allowed to.

sentences.zh: 尋爲著作佐郎兼權考功郎官。

translations.literal: Soon he was made assistant compiler and acting reviewer in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made assistant compiler with acting rank as personnel reviewer.

sentences.zh: 嘗因閔雨求言，乃上封事，謂：「今日有更化之名，無更化之實。

translations.literal: Once when drought was mourned and opinions were sought, he submitted a sealed memorial, saying, "Today there is the name of renewal but not the reality of renewal.
translations.idiomatic: When the court sought advice during a drought, he submitted a sealed memorial: "Today there is talk of renewal but no renewal in fact.

sentences.zh: 人才，國之元氣，而忠鯁擯廢之士，死者未盡省錄，存者未悉褒揚。

translations.literal: Talent is the vital energy of the state, yet loyal and upright men who were driven out—the dead have not all been posthumously recorded, the living have not all been praised and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Talent is the state's vital breath, yet loyal men who were cast out—the dead have not all been posthumously honored, the living not all rewarded.

sentences.zh: 言論，國之風采，其間輸忠亡隱，有所規益者，豈惟獎激弗加，蓋亦罕見施用；

translations.literal: Remonstrance is the state's bearing; among those who offered loyalty without concealment and had counsel to benefit, not only were rewards not added—they were rarely employed;
translations.idiomatic: Free speech is the state's dignity. Those who spoke frankly for the public good were not only unrewarded—they were rarely employed at all.

sentences.zh: 偷安取容，無所建明者，豈惟黜罰弗及，或乃遂階通顯。」

translations.literal: those who sought ease and curried favor and had nothing to propose—not only were they not dismissed and punished, some even ascended to high prominence."
translations.idiomatic: Those who sought ease and curried favor, offering nothing of value, were not punished—some even rose to high office."
