sentences.zh: 至若勉聖學以廣聰明，教儲貳以固根本，戒宰輔大臣同寅盡瘁以濟艱難，責侍從臺諫思職盡規以宣壅蔽，防左右近習竊弄之漸，察姦憸餘黨窺伺之萌，皆懇懇爲上言之。

translations.literal: As for urging sacred learning to broaden intelligence, instructing the heir to firm the foundation, warning chief ministers to exhaust themselves together in hardship, charging attendant ministers and censor-remonstrators to think on their duties and fully remonstrate to clear obstruction, guarding against the gradual usurpation of power by close attendants, and observing the sprouts of treacherous faction remnants watching for opportunity—all these he earnestly spoke to the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: He earnestly urged the emperor to pursue learning, train the heir, warn chief ministers to exhaust themselves in service, hold remonstrators to their duty, guard against favorites seizing power, and watch for remnants of the old faction—all spoken with full sincerity.

sentences.zh: 請外，知江州。

translations.literal: He asked to go outside and was made prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for an outside post and was made prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 郡民歲苦和糴，崇憲疏於朝，永蠲之。

translations.literal: The prefecture's people yearly suffered from harmonized purchase; Chongxian memorialized the court and had it permanently exempted.
translations.idiomatic: The people yearly suffered from government grain purchases. Chongxian memorialized the court and won permanent exemption.

sentences.zh: 且轉糴旁郡穀別廩儲之，以備歲儉。

translations.literal: Moreover he transferred grain purchased from neighboring prefectures and stored it in separate granaries to prepare for years of scarcity.
translations.idiomatic: He also bought grain from neighboring prefectures and stored it in separate granaries against famine.

sentences.zh: 瑞昌民負茶引錢，新舊累積，爲緡十七萬有奇，皆困不能償，死則以責其子孫猶弗貸。

translations.literal: The people of Ruichang owed tea certificate money; old and new accumulated to more than one hundred and seventy thousand strings of cash; all were distressed and unable to repay; when they died the debt was charged to sons and grandsons and still not forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: Ruichang people owed tea certificate debts totaling more than 170,000 strings of cash. All were crushed and could not pay. Death only passed the debt to their children and grandchildren without relief.

sentences.zh: 會新券行，視舊價幾倍蓰，崇憲歎曰：「負茶之民愈困矣。」

translations.literal: When new certificates were issued, compared with the old price they were several times higher; Chongxian sighed and said, "The tea-debt people will be more distressed."
translations.idiomatic: When new certificates were issued at several times the old price, Chongxian sighed, "The tea debtors will be crushed still further."

sentences.zh: 亟請以新券一償舊券二，詔從之。

translations.literal: He urgently asked that one new certificate redeem two old ones; an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: He urgently asked that one new certificate redeem two old ones. The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 蓋受賜者千餘家，刻石以紀其事。

translations.literal: In all more than a thousand households received the benefit, and they carved stone to record the affair.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand households benefited, and they carved a stone monument to record it.

sentences.zh: 修陂塘以廣溉灌，凡數千所。

translations.literal: He repaired dikes and ponds to broaden irrigation—several thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired dikes and ponds to expand irrigation—several thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 提舉江西常平兼權隆興府及帥漕司事，遷轉運判官仍兼帥事。

translations.literal: He was made commissioner of Jiangxi ever-normal granaries and concurrently acting for Longxing Prefecture and the military transport commissioner's affairs, then moved to transport commissioner while still concurrently commanding military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Jiangxi ever-normal commissioner with concurrent duties in Longxing and the military transport office, then transport commissioner while retaining military command.

sentences.zh: 初，汝愚捐私錢百餘萬創養濟院，俾四方賓旅之疾病者得藥與食，歲久寖移爲它用。

translations.literal: Earlier Ruyu donated more than a million in private funds to found a hospice so that traveling guests from the four directions who fell ill could obtain medicine and food; over the years it gradually shifted to other uses.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ruyu had donated more than a million in private funds to found a hospice for sick travelers from afar. Over the years its funds had been diverted.

sentences.zh: 崇憲至，尋修復，立規約數十條，以愈疾之多寡爲賞罰。

translations.literal: When Chongxian arrived, he soon restored it, established several tens of regulations, and made rewards and punishments according to how many patients recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongxian arrived he soon restored it, drew up dozens of regulations, and rewarded staff by how many patients recovered.

sentences.zh: 棄兒于道者，亦收鞠之。

translations.literal: Abandoned children on the roads he also took in and reared.
translations.idiomatic: He also took in abandoned children found on the roads.

sentences.zh: 社倉久敝，訪其利害而更張之。

translations.literal: The community granaries had long been dilapidated; he investigated their advantages and harms and reformed them.
translations.idiomatic: The community granaries had long fallen into disrepair. He investigated their workings and reformed them.

sentences.zh: 以兵部郎中召，尋改司封，皆固辭，遂直祕閣、知靜江府、廣西經略安撫。

translations.literal: He was summoned as director in the Ministry of War, soon changed to the Department of Seals, firmly declined both, and was then made rectifier in the Secretariat, prefect of Jingjiang, and Guangxi military commissioner and pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as director in the Ministry of War, then offered the Department of Seals, declined both, and was made Secretariat rectifier, prefect of Jingjiang, and Guangxi military commissioner and pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 靜江之屬邑十，地肥磽略等，而陽朔、修仁、荔浦之賦獨倍焉。

translations.literal: Jingjiang had ten subordinate counties; the land's fertility and barrenness were roughly equal, yet the tax levies of Yangshuo, Xiuren, and Lipu alone were doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjiang had ten subordinate counties of roughly equal land quality, yet Yangshuo, Xiuren, and Lipu alone paid double the tax.

sentences.zh: 自張栻奏減之餘，人猶以爲病。

translations.literal: Since Zhang Shi's memorial to reduce them, people still considered it a hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Even after Zhang Shi's memorial to reduce them, the burden was still considered oppressive.

sentences.zh: 崇憲請再加蠲減，詔遞損有差，三縣民立祠刻石。

translations.literal: Chongxian asked for further exemption and reduction; an edict ordered staged reductions by degree, and the people of the three counties erected shrines and carved stone.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxian asked for further reductions. An edict ordered staged cuts by degree, and the people of the three counties erected shrines and carved monuments.

sentences.zh: 瓊守非才，激黎峒之變，乃劾去之，改辟能者代其任。

translations.literal: The Qiongzhou prefect lacked ability and provoked trouble among the Li stockades; Chongxian impeached and removed him and recruited a capable man to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiongzhou prefect lacked ability and provoked unrest among the Li stockades. Chongxian impeached him and recruited a capable replacement.

sentences.zh: 蘿蔓峒者仍歲寇鈔爲暴，實民何向父子陰誘導之。

translations.literal: Those of Luoman stockade year after year raided and plundered violently; in fact the commoner He Xiang and his son secretly incited and guided them.
translations.idiomatic: Luoman stockade raided year after year. In fact a local man, He Xiang, and his son secretly incited them.

sentences.zh: 崇憲捐金繒付小校使繫以來，置之法。

translations.literal: Chongxian donated gold and silk to a petty officer to have them seized and brought in, and punished them by law.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxian paid gold and silk to a petty officer to seize them and bring them in, then punished them by law.

sentences.zh: 因嚴民夷交通之禁，使邊民相什伍，寇至則鳴鼓召衆，先後掩擊，俘獲者賞，不至者有懲。

translations.literal: Thereupon he strictly enforced the ban on intercourse between commoners and tribes, made border people form groups of ten and five, and when raiders came sounded drums to summon the crowd for successive ambush strikes; captors were rewarded, those who did not come were punished.
translations.idiomatic: He strictly enforced the ban on unauthorized contact between settlers and tribes, organized border people in groups of ten and five, and when raiders came sounded drums to summon them for ambush. Captors were rewarded; absentees punished.

sentences.zh: 先是，部內郡邑有警，輒移統府兵戍之，在宜州者百人，古縣半之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when counties within the jurisdiction had alarms, troops of the overall command were always transferred to garrison them—in Yizhou a hundred men, in Guxian half that.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when counties in his jurisdiction had alarms, troops from the overall command were posted as garrisons—one hundred at Yizhou, half that at Guxian.

sentences.zh: 崇憲謂根本單虛，非所以窒姦萌，乃於其地各置兵如戍兵之數，而斂戍者以歸。

translations.literal: Chongxian said the root was isolated and empty and this was not how to block treachery at its sprout; he therefore stationed troops in each place in numbers like the garrison troops and gathered the garrison detachments back.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxian said leaving the interior bare was no way to stop trouble at its root. He posted permanent garrisons in each place and recalled the roaming detachments.

sentences.zh: 邕爲邊要害地，自狄青平儂智高，所以設捍防者甚至，歲久浸弛，而溪峒日強。

translations.literal: Yong was a key frontier place; since Di Qing pacified Nong Zhigao, the defenses set up were very extensive; over the years they gradually slackened while the stream stockades grew stronger day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was a vital frontier post. Since Di Qing pacified Nong Zhigao its defenses had been extensive, but over the years they slackened while the hill tribes grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 崇憲條上其議，朝廷頗采其言，然未及盡用也。

translations.literal: Chongxian itemized and submitted his proposals; the court largely adopted his words, yet did not fully employ them.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxian submitted detailed proposals. The court largely adopted them but did not fully implement them.

sentences.zh: 崇憲天性篤孝，居父喪，月餘始食食，小祥始茹果實，終喪不飲酒食肉，比御猶弗入者久之。

translations.literal: Chongxian by nature was deeply filial; in his father's mourning, after more than a month he began to eat food, at the small felicitation he first tasted fruit, through the whole mourning he did not drink wine or eat meat, and for a long time he would not even enter the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxian was deeply filial by nature. During his father's mourning he ate no solid food for more than a month, tasted no fruit until the small felicitation, drank no wine and ate no meat through the full mourning period, and for a long time would not even enter the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自昔大臣處危疑之地，而能免於禍難者蓋鮮矣。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: From of old, great ministers placed in perilous and doubtful positions who could escape calamity have been few.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: From antiquity, few great ministers placed in peril and doubt have escaped disaster.

sentences.zh: 昔者周成王立而幼沖，周公以王室懿親爲宰輔，四國流言，而周公不免于居東之憂，非天降風雷之變，以彰周公之德而啟成王之衷，則所謂《金滕》之書，固無因而關於王之耳目，公之心果能以自明乎？

translations.literal: Formerly when King Cheng of Zhou was established while young and in his minority, the Duke of Zhou as a close kin of the royal house served as chief minister; the four states spread slander, and the Duke of Zhou could not avoid the worry of dwelling in the east. Had heaven not sent the transformation of wind and thunder to manifest the Duke of Zhou's virtue and open King Cheng's heart, then the so-called document in the Metal-bound Coffer would have had no way to reach the king's ears and eyes—could the Duke's heart truly have cleared itself?
translations.idiomatic: When King Cheng of Zhou came to the throne as a minor, the Duke of Zhou, the royal house's closest kin, served as regent. The four quarters spread slander, and the duke could not escape the ordeal of dwelling in the east. Had heaven not sent wind and thunder to manifest his virtue and open the young king's heart, how would the Metal-bound Coffer document ever have reached the king? Could the duke truly have cleared his own name?

sentences.zh: 公之心能自明，則天意之所以屬於周而綿八百載之丕祚者，實係於茲。

translations.literal: If the Duke's heart could clear itself, then heaven's reason for entrusting Zhou and extending its great fortune for eight hundred years truly hinged on this.
translations.idiomatic: Whether the duke could clear his name was whether heaven's mandate to Zhou—and eight hundred years of greatness—would stand.

sentences.zh: 不然，周其殆哉！

translations.literal: Otherwise, Zhou would have been in peril!
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise Zhou would have perished!

sentences.zh: 趙汝愚，宋之宗臣也，其賢固不及周公，其位與戚又非若周公之尊且昵也。

translations.literal: Zhao Ruyu was a dynastic minister of the Song; his worth certainly did not reach the Duke of Zhou's, and his position and kinship were not so honored and intimate as the Duke's.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ruyu was an imperial clansman of the Song. His virtue fell far short of the Duke of Zhou's, and his rank and kinship were neither so lofty nor so close.

sentences.zh: 方孝宗崩，光宗疾，大喪無主，中外洶洶，一時大臣有畏難而去者矣。

translations.literal: Just as Xiaozong died, Guangzong was ill, the great mourning had no master, within and without there was uproar, and among the chief ministers of the time were those who feared difficulty and left.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong died, Guangzong was ill, mourning had no chief, and the realm was in uproar. Some chief ministers fled from the danger.

sentences.zh: 汝愚獨能奮不慮身，定大計於頃刻，收召明德之士，以輔寧宗之新政，天下翕然望治，其功可謂盛矣。

translations.literal: Ruyu alone could rouse himself without considering his person, settle the great plan in a moment, recall and summon men of bright virtue to assist Ningzong's new government—the realm together looked to good order, and his merit can be called magnificent.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu alone acted without regard for his life, settled the succession in an instant, and recalled worthy men to assist Ningzong's new reign. The realm looked to good government. His achievement was magnificent.

sentences.zh: 然不幾時，卒爲韓侂胄所構，一斥而遂不復返，天下聞而冤之。

translations.literal: Yet before long he in the end was framed by Han Tuozhou, once driven out and never returning, and all under heaven heard and deemed it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Yet within little time he was framed by Han Tuozhou, driven out once, and never returned. The realm heard and judged it a grievous wrong.

sentences.zh: 于此見天之所以眷宋者不如周，而宋之陵夷馴至於不可爲，信非人力之所能也。

translations.literal: From this one sees that heaven's favor toward the Song was not like that toward Zhou, and the Song's decline gently reaching the point where nothing could be done was truly not within human power.
translations.idiomatic: Here one sees that heaven favored the Song less than Zhou, and the Song's gradual decline to ruin was truly beyond human power to reverse.

sentences.zh: 汝愚父以純孝聞，而子崇憲能守家法，所至有惠政，亦可謂世濟其美者已。

translations.literal: Ruyu's father was known for pure filial piety, and his son Chongxian could keep the family law; wherever he went there was benevolent government—this too can be called passing down the family's excellence through generations.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu's father was famed for pure filial piety. His son Chongxian upheld the family tradition and brought benevolent government wherever he served—a true heir to that excellence through the generations.
